full_text_en:
Dalian Fengqi Investment Management Co., Ltd. v. Sinotrans Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over loan contract

Ruling Summary

1. In the trial of a dispute over a chattel pledge supervision contract, the basic facts of whether the pledged property was actually delivered for supervision or was delivered in full amount for supervision shall be ascertained, and on this basis, an accurate determination shall be made as to whether the corresponding pledge right has been established.

2. In a dispute over a chattel pledge supervision contract, if the creditor, the debtor as the pledgor, and the pledge supervisor are all at fault for the pledged property not being actually delivered for supervision or not being delivered in full amount for supervision, then all three parties shall be liable for the losses caused to the creditor by the failure to establish the corresponding pledge right. Since the debtor bears the statutory obligation to deliver the pledged property and whether the pledged property is delivered directly determines the establishment of the pledge right, the debtor shall bear primary fault and primary liability for the losses caused to the creditor by the failure to establish the pledge right due to the pledged property not being actually delivered for supervision or not being delivered in full amount for supervision. Although the supervisor is at fault for mistakenly believing that the pledged property was actually delivered, because such fault is not the main cause of the failure to establish the pledge right, the supervisor shall bear secondary liability for the creditor's losses. Such liability of the supervisor arises from a breach of agreed obligations and shall be characterized as liability for breach of contract in nature.

3. In a dispute over a chattel pledge supervision contract, the creditor's direct obligors are the debtor and the guarantor, and the supervisor is only an auxiliary person assisting the creditor in realizing its credit rights. Except where the pledged property is lost due to the supervisor's own actions, the supervisor's liability shall be dependent on the direct liability of the debtor and the guarantor. If the direct liability is extinguished by satisfaction, and the creditor suffers no loss because it has been satisfied, the supervisor's supervision liability shall be correspondingly extinguished. Therefore, the supervisor is only a supplementary obligor to the aforementioned direct obligors, and shall bear supplemental compensation liability for the losses caused to the creditor by the failure to establish the pledge right due to the pledged property not being actually delivered for supervision or not being delivered in full amount for supervision.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2016) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Judgment No. 650

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Sinotrans Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. Domicile: No. 437, Houge Street, Ganjingzi District, Dalian, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Yingjie, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Gang, lawyer of Liaoning Yipin Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Dalian Fengqi Investment Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room B4-1-27-6, East Tower, No. 311, Changjiang Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Li Qi, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Song Chunjie, lawyer of Beijing Anli Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yang Yun, lawyer of Beijing Zhongman Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Dalian Harbor Grain Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 12, Wuwu Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Youwen, Chairman of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Dalian Port Co., Ltd. Domicile: Dayaowan New Port Business Building, Dalian Free Trade Zone, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Hui Kai, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Qing, lawyer of Liaoning Haida Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over loan contract between appellant Sinotrans Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company (hereinafter referred to as Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company) and appellee Dalian Fengqi Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fengqi Company), defendant at first instance Dalian Harbor Grain Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dalian Grain Company), and third party at first instance Dalian Port Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dalian Port Company), Fengqi Company filed a lawsuit with the Liaoning High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Liaoning High Court), which, after trial, rendered Civil Judgment (2014) Liao Min Er Chu Zi No. 00043 on November 12, 2014. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, dissatisfied, appealed to this Court. This Court, after trial, issued Civil Ruling (2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 155 on November 12, 2015, vacating the original judgment and remanding the case for retrial. Liaoning High Court, after retrial, rendered Civil Judgment (2016) Liao Min Chu No. 1 on June 21, 2016. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, still dissatisfied, appealed to this Court again. After accepting the case, this Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Zhang Nengbao of the Second Circuit Court and Judges Wang Guoxian and Dong Hua, with Judge Assistant Liu Yaoguo assisting in handling the case and Clerk Liu Meiyue recording, and held a public hearing on November 13, 2016. Agent ad litem Liu Gang of appellant Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company; Legal Representative Li Qi and agents ad litem Song Chunjie and Yang Yun of appellee Fengqi Company; and Agent ad litem Zhu Qing of Dalian Port Company appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. Dalian Grain Company, after being lawfully summoned by this Court, did not appear. The case has now been concluded.

At first instance, Fengqi Company alleged: On May 31, 2014, persons not party to this case, Yang Yi and Huang Jian, signed the Agreed upon Confirmation of Arrears and Assignment of Creditors' Rights Agreement with Dalian Grain Company, Dalian Guangde Grain Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangde Company), and Fengqi Company, agreeing that Yang Yi would assign to Fengqi Company the principal and interest of his claim against Guangde Company totaling RMB 55.8 million, and debtor Guangde Company confirmed such assignment of claim; Huang Jian would assign to Fengqi Company all of his claims against Dalian Grain Company, totaling principal and interest of RMB 74.4 million, and Dalian Grain Company confirmed such assignment of claim. On the same day, Fengqi Company, Dalian Grain Company, Guangde Company, and Liu Youwen, the actual controller of the latter two companies, signed the Agreement, agreeing that the debt of RMB 55.8 million owed by Guangde Company to Fengqi Company would be fully transferred to Dalian Grain Company. After the debt transfer, Fengqi Company held a claim of RMB 130.2 million against Dalian Grain Company. Dalian Grain Company promised to repay that day, failing which overdue interest would be paid at 2% per month. On the same day, Dalian Grain Company issued a Letter on Circumstances to Fengqi Company, stating that because Dalian Grain Company and its affiliated company Guangde Company had borrowed a total principal of RMB 208 million from four individuals, Yang Yi, Huang Jian, Li Qi, and Cui Yang, Dalian Grain Company intended to create a pledge of warehouse receipts for 145,400 tons of corn owned by Dalian Grain Company to the above four creditors. However, because Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company disagreed to sign a Pledge Supervision Agreement with individuals, only agreeing to sign with legal persons, the four creditors accordingly assigned all corresponding claims to Fengqi Company. Fengqi Company would sign the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement with Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company and Dalian Grain Company. On June 1, 2014, the Agreement signed by Cui Yang, Dalian Grain Company, and Fengqi Company stipulated that Cui Yang would assign his claim against Dalian Grain Company, totaling principal and interest of RMB 3 million, to Fengqi Company, and Dalian Grain Company promised to repay that day, failing which overdue interest would be paid at 2% per month. On June 5, 2014, the Agreement signed by Li Qi, Dalian Grain Company, and Fengqi Company stipulated that Li Qi would assign his claim against Dalian Grain Company, totaling principal and interest of RMB 130 million, to Fengqi Company, and Dalian Grain Company confirmed such assignment. After the completion of the above assignment agreements, Fengqi Company held claims against Dalian Grain Company totaling principal and interest of RMB 263.2 million.

On June 4, 2014, Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company signed the Maximum Amount Chattel Pledge Contract, agreeing that Dalian Grain Company would provide a pledge of its own corn to secure the above principal and interest of the loan, with a maximum secured amount of RMB 300 million. The pledged property was 145,400 tons of corn, provisionally valued at RMB 300 million. On the same day, Fengqi Company, Dalian Grain Company, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company signed the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement numbered ZhiYa FQ001, agreeing that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company would receive the pledged property delivered by Dalian Grain Company and issue a Written Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property (in Lieu of List of Pledged Property) (hereinafter referred to as Written Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property) to Fengqi Company; the pledged property would be transferred into possession, and the pledged property actually delivered for possession would be as specified in the Written Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property. The supervision period would commence from the time Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company received the pledged property. During the supervision period, unless confirmed in writing by Fengqi Company, the pledged property could not be removed from the warehouse or depot. If Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company violated the above provisions, it would bear corresponding compensation liability. When Fengqi Company exercised its pledge right, it should issue a release notice with Fengqi Company as the consignee to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, which should promptly handle the release of the pledged property. During the supervision period, if the pledged property deteriorated, diminished in quantity, or was lost due to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's failure to fulfill its supervision duties, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should compensate Fengqi Company. After signing the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company issued a Written Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property to Fengqi Company, clearly stating that it had received 145,400 tons of corn as pledged property and that the pledged property was under its possession and supervision. On June 9, 2014, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company collected a supervision fee of RMB 1.5 million. After signing the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement, because Dalian Grain Company was in financial difficulty and could not repay the above debts on the agreed date, it applied for an extension of repayment and submitted a Deferred Repayment Application to Fengqi Company in July 2014. Dalian Grain Company promised to fully perform its repayment obligation to Fengqi Company by July 15, 2014, and if it defaulted, Fengqi Company could directly exercise the pledge right.

In July 2014, because Dalian Grain Company failed to perform its repayment obligation, Fengqi Company repeatedly went to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company to confirm the status of the pledged property. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company confirmed that the pledged property was under its supervision and issued signed work records on chattel pledge supervision. The on-site supervisor issued a site inspection record to prove that the pledged property existed and was intact, and promised that as long as Fengqi Company issued a release notice, the pledged property would be delivered to Fengqi Company. Fengqi Company exercised its pledge right in accordance with the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement and issued a Release Notice to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, requesting Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company to handle the release procedures for the 145,400 tons of corn pledged property. However, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company refused to deliver the pledged property to Fengqi Company on the grounds that it had not contacted Dalian Grain Company. Based on this, Fengqi Company believed that: Dalian Grain Company failed to perform its repayment obligation in accordance with the loan agreement, constituting a breach of contract; Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company failed to perform its supervision obligation and its obligation to deliver the pledged property to Fengqi Company in accordance with the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement, constituting a breach of contract; the actions of Dalian Grain Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company had seriously infringed upon Fengqi Company's lawful rights and interests, and they should bear corresponding liability. Therefore, Fengqi Company filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting judgment: 1. That Dalian Grain Company repay Fengqi Company the outstanding debt of RMB 263.2 million and overdue interest (the loan principal and overdue interest to be repaid by Dalian Grain Company: RMB 263.2 million. Overdue payment interest to be calculated at a monthly rate of 2% from June 5, 2014 to the date of actual repayment. As of the first filing date in July 2014, overdue interest was RMB 7.896 million, and subsequent overdue interest is also within the scope of the claim); 2. That Fengqi Company be entitled to priority satisfaction from the proceeds of disposal of the pledged property; 3. That Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company bear joint and several compensation liability for the debt owed by Dalian Grain Company up to RMB 300 million; 4. That Dalian Grain Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company jointly bear all litigation costs and preservation costs of this case.

Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company argued in its defense at first instance: It disagreed with Fengqi Company's claims 2, 3, and 4 raised against Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. The specific reasons were as follows:

(1) The premise for Fengqi Company's request to dispose of the pledged property may not exist, and its second claim may be difficult to establish. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was not the liable party at the time of the pledge and should not bear legal liability. The legal nature of the grain at issue evolved from goods to pledged property and then to supervised property. According to the dates recorded in the railway consignment notes, the measurement notices for inbound port goods, and the grain quality inspection reports, the grain at issue had already entered the storage location in March-April 2014, while supervision began on June 4, 2014. When this batch of goods was pledged to Fengqi Company, Fengqi Company already knew in advance the existence condition of the grain. In its complaint, it admitted that it intended to create a pledge of Dalian Grain Company's 145,400 tons of corn to the four individual creditors, but because Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company disagreed to sign a pledge supervision agreement with individuals, only agreeing to sign with legal persons, the four creditors accordingly assigned all corresponding claims to Fengqi Company, and Fengqi Company signed the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement with Dalian Grain Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. Thus, Fengqi Company only signed the maximum amount pledge contract with Dalian Grain Company after being told by Dalian Grain Company that it had grain available for pledge and verifying Dalian Grain Company's goods. The pledge contract clearly stipulated provisions on the realization of the pledge right and the return of the pledged property, and the chattel pledge list attached to the contract clearly recorded the name, quantity, value, and insurance policy number of the pledged property. These actions all demonstrate that Fengqi Company, as the pledgee, had the duty to inspect and receive the pledged property. Such inspection and receipt occurred before supervision and were unrelated to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's supervision actions. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should not assume contractual obligations at this stage. Analyzing from the legal concepts of delivery and possession, the owner of the grain at issue, Dalian Grain Company, delivered the grain to the depositor, Dalian Xingang Harbor International Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xingang Logistics Company). Xingang Logistics Company stored the received grain in the warehouse of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company, the user of the site under agreement. The in-and-out warehouse operations of that warehouse were all controlled by Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, in accordance with the supervision agreement, conducted surface review, appearance inspection, and document verification of the pledged grain and began supervision. There was no actual delivery of grain to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. In summary, if the grain did exist, Dalian Grain Company's delivery to Xingang Logistics Company was an actual delivery. Xingang Logistics Company and Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company were the actual possessors of the goods. Even if Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company claimed possession, it was only indirect possession, unable to directly control the pledged property. Therefore, if Fengqi Company wished to retrieve the pledged property and realize the pledge right, it should claim delivery from Xingang Logistics Company, the actual recipient of the delivery, and Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company, the actual possessor directly controlling the pledged property. The tripartite supervision agreement also so provided. Article 7 of the supervision agreement stipulated the procedure for exercising the pledge right: first, Fengqi Company would issue a release notice to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, which would provide necessary cooperation and assistance; such cooperation and assistance consisted of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company signing a receipt for the release notice and notifying the warehouser to release the goods. Throughout the entire process, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was not responsible for the actual delivery of goods. If the goods did not exist at the time of the pledge's creation, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should not have any contractual obligations or legal liability. Fengqi Company's second and third claims were contradictory and conflicting. The second claim requested disposal of the pledged property, the premise of which was clearly that Fengqi Company itself believed the pledged property existed. The third claim requested Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company to bear joint and several compensation liability within the scope of the debt of RMB 300 million, the premise of which was clearly that the pledged property no longer existed and could not be delivered. In summary, combined with the existing evidence, it was highly likely that the grain at issue did not exist from the very beginning of the pledge, and Fengqi Company was also aware of this situation. Fengqi Company was simply unwilling to bear responsibility for its own negligence and fault, and unwilling to pursue criminal proceedings for Dalian Grain Company's liability for contract fraud, instead attempting to expand liability to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company by filing a civil action. However, its claims lacked factual and legal basis. As a legal person enterprise, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company did not participate in contract fraud and had no contractual obligations or legal liability for the false pledge behavior that existed before supervision.

(2) As Fengqi Company's mandatory agent, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company fulfilled its duties in accepting the entrusted supervision business and should not bear compensation liability. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's liability in this case was to perform obligations and bear legal liability in accordance with the provisions of the tripartite supervision agreement. According to the supervision agreement, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was entrusted by Fengqi Company to supervise. Its duties were only to properly keep the title certificates of the goods during the supervision period, monitor the quantity of goods, and supervise the behavior of the owner of the goods. Once it discovered that the pledgor, Dalian Grain Company, or the warehouser, Xingang Logistics Company, had unauthorizedly retrieved or released goods in violation of this agreement, it had the duty to promptly stop such conduct and report to Fengqi Company. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was not the custodian or direct controller of the goods. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company exercised supervision over the goods that had been confirmed by both Fengqi Company and the owner to be in the warehouse. If during this period there were no acts of fault or intent such as unauthorized release, release without documents, or collusion with others to release goods, it should not bear contractual liability.

(3) The Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement signed between Fengqi Company, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, and Dalian Grain Company was invalid, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should not bear legal liability. Based on the existing evidence, the pledged property was not stored in the warehouse of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company at all. Therefore, the pledge under the pledge guarantee contract between Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company was not effective. The pledge supervision agreement was concluded and took effect on the premise that the pledge was valid. If the pledge guarantee contract was invalid, the purpose of the pledge supervision agreement could not be achieved, and it should be rescinded. Given that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was subjected to fraud, the pledge supervision agreement should be revoked. Since the pledged property did not exist, Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company, knowing this, conspired to defraud Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company and induce its supervision. Therefore, the pledge supervision agreement signed among the three parties should be revoked, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should not bear contractual liability.

(4) The pledge contract between Fengqi Company and Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. in this case is a pledge of rights, not a pledge of movables. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. has fulfilled its responsibilities in the custody and storage of the documents and has not committed any breach. According to the provisions of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, the most fundamental characteristic of a pledge of movables is the transfer of possession of the movables, and the transfer of possession is also a requirement for the validity of a pledge contract of movables. In this case, Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. should have delivered the 145,401 tons of corn to Fengqi Company for possession. However, as a matter of objective fact, all the goods involved in this case were stored at Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd. and Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd., and were directly possessed by Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd. and indirectly possessed by Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd. Fengqi Company never possessed the goods. Therefore, although the relevant contract was described as a pledge of movables, the pledge contract of movables did not take effect because the necessary requirements for the validity of the pledge of movables were lacking. If the pledge contract is valid, it should be a pledge of rights. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. believes that the so-called pledge of rights in this case is a pledge of warehouse receipts. Although the warehouseman in this case did not issue formal warehouse receipts to the depositor, in light of the specific business operation process of this case, the following documents can collectively constitute de facto warehouse receipts: 1. The cargo position charts confirmed by Dalian Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd. and Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd.; 2. The grain quality inspection reports jointly confirmed by Dalian Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd., Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd., and the cargo owner Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd.; 3. The warehouse entry receipts jointly confirmed by Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd. and the cargo owner Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd.; 4. The railway waybills for the transportation of goods into the port; 5. The "Notice of Inbound Cargo Measurement" (commonly known as the weighbridge slip) stamped with the seals of the Dayaowan Station track scale of Dalian Port Railway Company, Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd., and Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd.; 6. The "Notice of Type, Price, and Minimum Requirements for the Pledged Property (Substitute Notice of Pledge)" (hereinafter referred to as the "Substitute Notice of Pledge") jointly confirming by Fengqi Company and Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. that the goods were already in the warehouse. Collectively, these documents are essentially delivery documents with the nature of warehouse receipts. In particular, the weighbridge slips and warehouse entry receipts can fully serve as documents for the right holder to take delivery of the goods. In the business of this case, the parties further agreed on the process and documents for taking delivery of the goods, namely, Fengqi Company was required to issue a "Notice of Release of Goods" to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. After verification with no errors, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. would handle the delivery procedures for the right holder and, after issuing a "Warehouse Outbound Operation Notice," complete the supervision of the corresponding goods. Pursuant to the notification in the "Substitute Notice of Pledge," Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. supervised the goods that Fengqi Company had confirmed were already in the warehouse and kept the aforementioned documents 1-5. Prior to the actual supervision by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd., the fact that the goods were already in the warehouse had been jointly confirmed by Fengqi Company and Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. Fengqi Company simultaneously handed over all documents to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. After reviewing all documents, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. diligently performed its duties. It never released goods without Fengqi Company's consent, never issued a "Pledged Property Warehouse Outbound Operation Slip" to any third party, and never transferred the rights documents of the goods to others. Not a single document in its custody was lost; all were intact. The supervisor fully fulfilled its obligations and did not cause any loss to Fengqi Company. According to the nature of a pledge of rights and the characteristics of the silos of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd., Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. was not required and was unable to take possession and control of the movables themselves. In the event that the rights documents are intact but the pledged property is short or lost, the pledgee can only pursue liability against the party responsible for the shortage or loss based on the pledge documents, which has nothing to do with Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd.

(5) There is no causal relationship between Fengqi Company's inability to recover the loan on time and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. According to the evidence provided by Fengqi Company, Fengqi Company's lending of funds to Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. occurred prior to the supervision business involved in this case. Fengqi Company, regardless of commercial risk, voluntarily lent a huge amount of money to Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. without any guarantee, resulting in bad debt risk. This risk and the ultimate loss have no direct causal connection with the supervision behavior of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. According to the investigation conducted by the court of first instance with Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd. and the statements of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd., Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. did not store grain at Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal or conduct business there. Why did Fengqi Company inform Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. through the "Substitute Notice of Pledge" that the goods were already in the warehouse? Could Fengqi Company be colluding with Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. to defraud Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. into providing supervision? If the pledged property did not exist at all, then the pledge contract of movables should not take effect. If the pledged property did not exist, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. provided supervision in the absence of a supervision target and as a result of fraud that vitiated its true intention, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. has the right to rescind the supervision agreement. If the fact that the goods never existed in the first place is established, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. will immediately assert the right to rescind the supervision agreement and disclaim supervision liability. In summary, there is no causal relationship between Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. and the consequences of Fengqi Company's inability to recover the loan. Fengqi Company can only resolve the private lending dispute with Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. on its own. If fraud is suspected, Fengqi Company should promptly report to the public security authorities and pursue the criminal liability of Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd.

(6) Fengqi Company's request for Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. to assume joint and several compensation liability within the scope of RMB 300 million lacks legal basis. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd.'s legal liability in this case is limited to the liability agreed in the supervision agreement. This legal liability is contractual liability. The prerequisite for assuming contractual liability is that the breach of contract has caused losses to the counterparty. The method of assuming liability is to compensate the compliant counterparty for losses. The legal basis is the provisions on breach of contract in the Contract Law. In this case, it is evident that it was because Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. violated the agreement by falsely pledging that the pledge right could not be realized. According to the principle of privity of contract, it should be Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. that assumes liability for breach of contract to both Fengqi Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd., rather than the compliant party assuming liability for breach of contract to the other compliant party. The joint and several compensation liability claimed by Fengqi Company is generally the legal liability for joint tort, as well as several situations explicitly provided by law, such as the joint and several liability of a surety, the joint and several liability of a principal and agent to a third party due to unclear written authorization, or liability arising from the parties' agreement. Fengqi Company's request for Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. to assume joint and several compensation liability does not fall under the aforementioned circumstances. The request to assume joint and several compensation liability has neither legal basis nor contractual basis.

(7) This case is a case of contract fraud and should be handled by the public security authorities. Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. has been investigated for loan fraud. Its act of using false pledges to gain the trust of the lender to obtain funds is identical in nature and pattern to its act in this case of using false pledges to gain the trust of the creditor to be released from debits. Furthermore, the Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court (2015) Min Er Chu Zi No. 155 requires the ascertainment of basic facts such as whether Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. provided the pledged property as stipulated in the contract, or whether it provided all the pledged property or only part of it. These facts cannot be accurately ascertained by the civil trial division alone without using investigative techniques by the public security authorities to locate and interview relevant personnel from Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd., Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd., Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd., and Dalian Port Railway Company. If these facts cannot be ascertained, the case cannot be resolved. In summary, whether from the nature of the case or from the approach to handling the case, only after the criminal case is concluded can the civil liability of each party be examined based on the results of the criminal investigation.

(8) In its complaint, Fengqi Company alleged that during the supervision period, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. failed to fulfill its supervision duties, resulting in deterioration or damage of the pledged property, which should lead to compensation liability. However, no such deterioration or damage occurred during the supervision period, so Fengqi Company's lawsuit is unfounded. Fengqi Company claimed that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. issued a "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property" informing Fengqi Company that the pledged property was under the supervision of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. This was merely a contractual act. The premise for issuing such notice was that Fengqi Company and Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. had issued a notice of pledge, which clearly stated that Fengqi Company had received the pledged property specifying its name and quantity, and that it was in the warehouse. Only then did Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. issue the "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property." This was a contractual action and did not involve actual delivery of the pledged property. Both parties were aware that the pledged property was stored in the warehouse of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal, and there was no actual delivery or physical possession. The allegations in the complaint are not factual. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. did not promise the actual delivery of the goods to Fengqi Company. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd.'s commitment, in accordance with the supervision agreement, was to issue a "Notice of Release of Goods," which Fengqi Company could use to take delivery from Xingang Logistics Co., Ltd. In summary, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd. believes that Fengqi Company's lawsuit seeking it to assume legal liability has no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed.

Dalian Port Company argued in its first-instance defense: Dalian Port Company has no interest in this case and requests the court to remove its status as a third party. The reasons are as follows: (1) In its complaint, Fengqi Company sued two defendants based on a loan contract dispute. Dalian Port Company is neither a defendant nor a party to this case, has no contractual relationship such as a loan with Fengqi Company, and has no legal interest in the matter. Dalian Port Company is completely unaware of the subject matter involved and does not possess the legal characteristics of a third party.

(2) The corn mentioned in Fengqi Company's complaint has nothing to do with Dalian Port Company, and there is no such grain stored as alleged. In this regard, the evidence determined by the Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court (2015) Min Er Chu Zi No. 155 shows that Sun Mou, an employee of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd., stated during an interrogation by the public security authorities that he had handled the supervision of 140,000 to 150,000 tons of corn pledged property for Fengqi Company. The pattern was the same as the criminal fraud case: under the direction of superiors, false supervision logs and itemized ledgers were fabricated to show that the grain existed and was under supervision, even though no grain was present. Clearly, this case involves criminal activity but has nothing to do with Dalian Port Company.

(3) Dalian Port Company notes that the cargo position chart in Fengqi Company's evidence is dated June 2014, and the seal of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd. on it is completely fake. This seal had already been declared obsolete due to severe wear and tear as of September 1, 2010, and was confiscated and destroyed by the public security department on the same day. The load tonnage shown on the cargo position chart provided by Fengqi Company is between 8,700 and 8,900 tons, whereas the maximum load capacity of the corresponding silo at Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Co., Ltd. is 840 tons and 3,500 tons—over 5,000 tons less than what Fengqi Company's chart indicates. It is obvious that the cargo position chart provided by Fengqi Company is forged. Dalian Port Company has no interest in this case and is not a third party. It requests the court to revoke its status as a third party and to protect its lawful rights and interests.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial: On May 17, 2013, Li Qi transferred RMB 100 million into the designated account of Dalian Cereals Co., Ltd. On the same day, Fengqi Company (Party A, pledgee), Dalian Grain Company (Party B, pledgor), and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company (Party C, supervisor), in view of the fact that Dalian Grain Company agreed to pledge the goods it owned to Fengqi Company, and Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company agreed to deliver the pledged property to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company for supervision, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company agreed to accept the entrustment of Fengqi Company and supervise the pledged property in accordance with the instructions of Fengqi Company, jointly entered into a Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement numbered Pledge FQ001. Among others, it was agreed: Article 1, the term "supervision" as used in this Agreement refers to the supervision of the pledgor and the monitoring of the pledged property. Supervision of the pledgor means supervising the pledgor's processes such as warehousing and withdrawal of the pledged property, and once any act in violation of this Agreement is discovered, Party C shall promptly stop it and report to Party A; monitoring of the pledged property means inspecting and verifying the name, quantity, etc. of the pledged property, timely reporting the condition of the pledged property to Party A, and if any discrepancy is found, Party C shall promptly report to Party A and take corresponding measures. Article 2, paragraph 6, provided that during the transfer of possession of the pledged property, Party A and Party B shall issue a Notice of Substituted Pledge to Party C in accordance with the pledge contract. If the goods delivered by Party B and the actual inventory match the records in the Notice of Substituted Pledge, Party C shall receive the goods delivered by Party B and issue a Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property to Party A, and the transfer of possession of the pledged property shall be completed. The pledged property actually transferred and delivered into possession shall be based on what is specified in the Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property. If the description of the pledged property in the pledge contract is unclear, or if the pledged property agreed upon is inconsistent with the pledged property actually delivered, the pledged property actually delivered into possession shall prevail. Article 2, paragraph 8, provided that if the goods delivered by Party B and the actual inventory are inconsistent with the records in the Notice of Substituted Pledge, Party C shall not receive the goods and issue a Notice of Receipt of Goods, and shall immediately notify both Party A and Party B in writing. Article 2, paragraph 10, provided that upon issuing the Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property, Party C shall also send to Party A a location identification diagram of the pledged property. Article 3, paragraph 2: Party C shall receive the goods submitted by Party B in accordance with this Agreement as provided in Article 2, paragraph 6, and issue the Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property. Upon completion of the transfer of possession, the supervision period shall commence. Article 4, paragraph 1, provided that, entrusted by Party A and with the consent of Party B, the supervisory services provided by Party C mainly included the following contents, and Party C assumed responsibility for these services: (1) establishing a dedicated project team to design a supervision plan, which after consultation and confirmation with Party A and Party B, shall be organized and implemented; (2) assigning supervisors at the supervision site to inspect, verify, and count the pledged property, and to obtain and record data on the condition of the pledged property; (3) regularly reporting data on the condition of the pledged property to Party A and Party B; (4) monitoring the pledged property, and upon discovering any shortage or other abnormal condition, promptly reporting to Party A and Party B, and taking appropriate and reasonable measures to stop and rectify; (5) supervising the processes of inbound and outbound warehousing by Party B, and upon discovering any violation of the requirements of this Agreement or any irregular behavior or other abnormal condition, promptly reporting to Party A and Party B, and requesting Party B to take measures to stop and rectify. Article 4, paragraph 3, provided that if there were special requirements for the storage of the pledged property, Party B shall notify Party C in writing in advance before submitting the goods. Article 4, paragraph 4, provided that during the supervision period, if, for any reason, the pledged property suffered from shortage, damage, deterioration, loss, or other circumstances that might affect the rights and interests of Party A, Party C shall notify Party A within 24 hours and take appropriate emergency measures. Article 4, paragraph 6, provided that during the supervision period, Party C shall accept inquiries from Party A regarding the pledged property and related documents, accept inspections of the pledged property by Party A, and provide necessary assistance. However, any related expenses incurred by Party C shall be borne by Party B. Article 4, paragraph 7, provided that during the supervision period, Party C shall establish a system for registering and counting the pledged property, regularly inspect and verify the types, count the quantities, check the packaging and markings of the pledged property, and record the time, quantity, destination, and current status of inbound and outbound warehousing of the pledged property. Article 4, paragraph 8, provided that during the supervision period, Party C shall store the pledged property in accordance with the location identification diagram issued to Party A, and shall separate the pledged goods of Party B from the goods of other customers; if the supervision site is Party B's premises, Party C shall supervise Party B to separate the pledged goods from other non-pledged goods; when the location of the pledged property is moved, the location identification diagram shall be updated in a timely manner. Article 4, paragraph 12, provided that Party C shall set up pledge identification marks on the relevant pledged property by affixing pledge labels or erecting identification plates. However, whether Party C established pledge identification marks on the pledged property in accordance with this provision did not affect the effectiveness of the pledge. Even if Party C did not set up pledge identification marks on the pledged property, the relevant pledge remained effective. Article 5, paragraph 2, provided that when the actual value of the pledged property equaled the minimum value required by Party A, Party B shall submit a withdrawal application to Party A in advance, and either add or supplement a deposit or repay the financing (i.e., pay to redeem the goods), or provide Party A with pledged property that conforms to the requirements of the Notice of Substituted Pledge and deliver it to Party C for possession and supervision (i.e., exchange goods for goods). With the consent of Party A, Party B may then handle the withdrawal with Party C based on the Notice of Release of Goods issued by Party A. Article 5, paragraph 3, provided that when the actual value of the pledged property equaled the minimum value of the pledged property, the Notice of Release of Goods issued by Party A was the only valid credential for Party B (including Party B's designees, hereinafter the same) to handle the withdrawal and the removal of the pledged property from the warehouse. Without a Notice of Release of Goods issued by Party A, Party B shall not withdraw the goods, and Party C shall not handle withdrawal procedures for Party B. Article 5, paragraph 5, provided that the valid signatures and seals for the Notice of Substituted Pledge, the Notice of Release of Goods, and the Notice of Adjustment of Pledged Property Price issued by Party A were the reserved seal plus the personal signature of the designated person. The reserved seal and signature sample were shown in Appendix 5. Unless the seal of Party A and the personal signature of the designated person were verified and found correct, the pledged property shall not be removed from the warehouse. If Party C violated the above provisions and allowed Party B to withdraw goods, Party C shall bear corresponding compensation liability. Article 10, paragraph 1, provided that no two of the three parties (A, B, and C) may use any agreement or contract between themselves to oppose the obligations that should be performed under this Agreement. Article 12, paragraph 1, provided that if Party C caused losses to Party A under the following circumstances, it shall bear compensation liability for Party A's actual losses, and Party A had priority in receiving compensation from the compensation amount for its actual losses: 1. During the supervision period, except for events of force majeure or Party B's failure to perform its obligations under Article 4, paragraph 3 of this Agreement, if due to Party C's failure to fulfill its supervisory duties, the pledged property deteriorated, became short, contaminated, or was damaged or lost; 2. Party C failed to handle the release of goods in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement; 4. Due to Party C's violation of Article 4, paragraph 4 of this Agreement, it failed to timely notify Party A and Party B or failed to take appropriate emergency measures; 5. Other circumstances where Party C caused losses to Party A due to its violation of this Agreement. Article 15, paragraph 2, provided that if the financing contract (or financing application), pledge contract, and other formal contracts or ancillary documents (in whole or in part) signed between Party A and Party B were determined to be invalid by a judicial authority, the validity of this Agreement was not affected.

On June 9, 2014, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company issued a receipt to Dalian Grain Company for supervision fees of RMB 1.5 million.

It was also found that: On June 4, 2014, in view of the fact that Dalian Grain Company, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, and Fengqi Company had signed the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement (No. Pledge FQ001), to perform this agreement, Xingang Logistics Company (Party A, warehouseman), Dalian Grain Company (Party B, depositor), and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company (Party C, supervisor) jointly signed a Warehousing Management Agreement.
