Article 4, paragraph 1, provided that Party C would review whether Party B's goods met the conditions for outbound warehousing in accordance with Party C's business procedures. Party C had independent judgment and review authority. Article 4, paragraph 3, provided that after Party C issued the Work Order for Inbound Pledged Property, Party A would arrange loading, unloading, and handling operations based on the operation instructions of Party C's on-site personnel.

On January 1, 2010, Xingang Logistics Company (Party A) and Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company (Party B) entered into an Agreement on the Use of Bulk Grain Silos, stipulating that Party B agreed to allocate the capacity of its 500,000-ton corn bulk grain silos to Party A as dedicated storage for corn goods. The ownership of the bulk grain silos belonged to Party B, and Party A had the right to use them. Dalian Port Company did not recognize this agreement and considered that Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company had never had a business relationship with Xingang Logistics Company, had never signed such an agreement, and had never leased out silo capacity externally in previous business dealings.

In February 2011, Xingang Logistics Company (Party A) and Dalian Grain Company (Party B) entered into a Warehousing and Storage Agreement, stipulating that Party B leased a warehouse from Party A for a term of five years (February 2011 to February 2016).

On June 26, 27, July 15, and 29, 2014, Fengqi Company repeatedly contacted Sun He of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, Supervisor Zhang Qiang stationed at Dayaowan Terminal, and Wang Yingjie, Deputy General Manager of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, to inquire about the existence of the pledged property. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company provided Fengqi Company with ledgers, location diagrams, general ledgers, and detailed ledgers, allowed Fengqi Company to take photographs for retention, and presented the handwritten inventory results by the supervisor, thereby confirming that the pledged property was under the supervision of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company and existed intact and undamaged.

It was further found that: During the first instance trial of this case, Fengqi Company filed an application for property preservation with the court, requesting the sealing of 145,400 tons of corn stored at the Xingang Logistics Warehouse at Dayaowan Bulk Grain Terminal in the Dalian Economic and Technological Development Zone, Liaoning Province. On September 12, 2014, the court issued a Notice of Assistance in Enforcement (No. (2014) Liao Er Min Chu Zhi Zi 00043) to Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company. On September 14, 2014, Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company stated clearly in the receipt of the notice: "Our company does not have the 'Xingang Logistics Warehouse at Dayaowan Bulk Grain Terminal' as stated in your court's Notice of Assistance in Enforcement. The companies mentioned in the notice have no grain stored in our company."

Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company did not have independent legal personality; it was affiliated with Dalian Port Company, and the rights and obligations of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company were assumed by Dalian Port Company. On September 1, 2010, the seal of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company with the suffix number 45 was applied for cancellation and reported to the public security authority for destruction.

The above facts were supported by the Debt Confirmation and Assignment Agreement, three Agreements, the Explanation of Circumstances, the Maximum Amount Chattel Pledge Contract, the Chattel Pledge Supervision Agreement and related documents, the receipt for payment, the property comprehensive insurance policy, the Late Payment Application, documentary evidence confirming the pledged property, the delivery order, the original loan document, video recordings and written records, and Document No. (2010) 45 of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company, which were verified through cross-examination and deemed sufficient for determination; the court adopted them.

Regarding the railway freight consignment notes, the inbound cargo measurement notices, the grain quality inspection reports for 14 silo compartments, the inbound warehouse orders, the location diagrams, the general ledger of goods, the inventory details, and the notification letter provided by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company: The railway freight consignment notes were dated April 2014, the grain quality inspection reports were dated January to April 2014, and the notification letter was dated June 3, 2014, which were contradictory in time; the notification letter and the cargo location diagram bore the seal of Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company with the suffix number 45, but Dalian Port Company confirmed that Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company had declared that seal as severely worn and invalid as early as September 1, 2010, and on the same day, it was confiscated and destroyed by the Zhongshan Branch of the Dalian Public Security Bureau; Dalian Port Company also did not recognize the authenticity of the above evidence. Therefore, it was impossible to determine whether the above evidence was related to the disputed facts of this case, and the court did not adopt it.

Liu Youwen, the legal representative of Dalian Grain Company, was currently detained in the Jilin Province Xinkang Prison on suspicion of contract fraud. Since his criminal case was being tried in the Changchun Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Changchun Intermediate Court), the first-instance court commissioned the Changchun Intermediate Court to interrogate Liu Youwen. During the interrogation, Liu Youwen admitted that after signing the Maximum Amount Chattel Pledge Contract with Fengqi Company, he did not deliver the pledged property of 145,400 tons of corn to Fengqi Company in accordance with the contract, and that Fengqi Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company knew that the 145,400 tons of corn as pledged property had never existed from the beginning.

Fengqi Company's cross-examination opinion on the interrogation record of Liu Youwen was: Liu Youwen's statement that Fengqi Company knew that the pledged property did not exist was inconsistent with the facts. Fengqi Company had no knowledge that the pledged property did not exist. The borrowings by Dalian Grain Company from Yang Yi, Huang Jian, Cui Yang, and Li Qi were used to repay the bank loans. At that time, Dalian Grain Company's borrowings from the bank were secured by corn as collateral. The pledged property in this case was originally under the supervision of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, and all pledge supervision procedures were handled by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. Without this bank loan, Fengqi Company would not have lent the money to Dalian Grain Company. Therefore, there was no issue of Dalian Grain Company first delivering the pledged property to Fengqi Company, which then transferred it to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. This corn had already been pledged and supervised, and it could not serve as collateral for financing from a third party. Dalian Grain Company failed to repay the loan in accordance with the repayment term of the loan contract. At that time, Dalian Grain Company had sufficient property under its name to pledge to Fengqi Company, but there was previously a corn pledge, and moreover, it was already under the supervision of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, making the pledge relatively convenient. Fengqi Company disagreed with Liu Youwen's statement that the pledged property did not exist. Fengqi Company believed the pledged property existed because the money it lent to Dalian Grain Company was bridge financing, and the corresponding pledged property was this corn, which was already under the supervision of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. When the contract was signed on June 4, 2014, in the office of Sun He, Manager of the Pledge Supervision Department of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, the legal representative of Fengqi Company, Li Qi, asked when they could go to inspect the goods. Sun He replied that the inspection had been completed, and Fengqi Company did not need to inspect; they should rely on Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's inspection. At that time, Fengqi Company, as required by Sun He, filled in on the "Notice of Substitute Pledge" that 145,400 tons of corn were in the warehouse. Sun He then immediately filled out the "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property" in his own handwriting, confirming receipt of 145,400 tons of corn as pledged property. On June 9, 2014, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company collected a supervision fee of RMB 1,500,000. Based on the feedback from Wang Yingjie and Sun He of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, as well as on-site supervisor Zhang Qiang, and the evidence materials regarding the existence of the pledged property, it was all proven that the pledged property existed. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company also proved that the pledged property existed. Wang Yingjie personally told the judge of the original first instance that the pledged property existed. During the original first instance, all parties agreed that the pledged property existed initially. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company believed that the loss of the pledged property was caused by Dalian Port Bulk Grain Terminal Company, so it requested the addition of a third party to bear the responsibility for the loss of the pledged property. The "Agreement on Pledge of Movable Property Supervision" explicitly stipulated that inspection of the goods was Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's obligation, not Fengqi Company's obligation.

Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's cross-examination opinion on the interrogation record of Liu Youwen was: Liu Youwen proved that 145,400 tons of corn did not exist. Fengqi Company knew that the pledged property did not exist. In this case, Dalian Grain Company's pledge was not genuine and was not intended to secure the debts in this case. Fengqi Company, in order to increase its own security and to secure high-interest financing, made Liu Youwen cooperate in issuing documents related to the pledge of the property. Fengqi Company knew that there was no pledged property, and therefore there was no basis for Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company to compensate for losses. Liu Youwen admitted to borrowing RMB 100,000,000, and not through the false pledge in this case as security. Therefore, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company did not recognize the authenticity of any evidence concerning RMB 263,200,000. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company believed that the existence of the pledged property was determined after verifying the documents, which was also the review method stipulated in the supervision agreement. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was not aware of the ownership of the pledged property; Fengqi Company was responsible for verifying the ownership of the pledged property. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company had no responsibility to check the actual existence of the grain. The "Notice of Substitute Pledge" was jointly issued by Dalian Grain Company and Fengqi Company. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company issued the list of pledged property based on that notice. If either of them now says there was no grain, it might be that there was none. This only proves that the documents were false, but it cannot be said that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company knew from the beginning that there was no grain; Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was defrauded. If this case involves a false pledge, the parties may be suspected of committing the crime of contract fraud. The court should transfer the legal relationship of the pledge contract to the public security organ for investigation.

Dalian Port Company's cross-examination opinion on the interrogation record of Liu Youwen was: This interrogation record further indicates that there was no grain involved at all. Dalian Port Company was completely unaware and had no connection with this case.

On September 18, 2014, the Economic Crime Investigation Detachment of the Changchun Public Security Bureau (another case) interrogated Sun Jiaguo of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company (copied from the case file of the Supreme People's Court (2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 155). The record stated: Q: Do you know why the public security organ has summoned you according to law? A: The pledged grain that I was responsible for supervising at the Dalian Dayaowan Bulk Grain Terminal does not exist. Q: How did you know? A: My company leaders repeatedly said that not a single grain could be seen, but we still had to make records. Q: The leaders said that not a single grain could be seen, but we still had to make records. Then in your opinion, does the pledged property you supervised actually exist? A: The leaders' meaning was very clear; there was simply no grain. Q: Since there was no grain, were the supervision logs and detailed ledgers you kept true? A: They could not be true. Q: What was the purpose of the accounts and logs you kept? A: They were to deal with the bank people. When people from Jilin Bank came to inspect the warehouse, they would look at the accounts and logs. Q: What was the purpose of looking at the accounts and supervision logs? A: They would think that there was grain on site and that the pledged property was fine. Q: You did not even know the location, and there was no grain in the warehouse. How did you prepare the logs and accounts? A: The leaders told us that even if there was no grain, we had to write, so I had to make up and fabricate things to prove that there was grain and that the grain was in a safe state. Q: At this bulk grain terminal, besides supervising the pledged property belonging to Jilin Bank, which other banks' pledged property did you supervise? A: There was also about 80,000 to 90,000 tons of corn for Harbin Bank, about 97,000 tons of corn for Fushun Bank, over 100,000 tons of corn for Dalian Bank, over 20,000 tons for Guangdong Development Bank Dalian Branch, about 10 tons of corn for Bank of China, 50,000 to 60,000 tons for Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, over 100,000 tons for Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, in addition to 140,000 to 150,000 tons for Fengqi Company, and 6,000 tons for Dalian Xinding Trading Company. Including Jilin Bank, there were 10 banks in total. Q: Was the model for the other nine banks the same as for Jilin Bank? A: All the same. There was also no grain. The leaders told us to fabricate accounts and logs. Q: Did your company leaders' requirement that "not a single grain can be seen, but we still have to make records" include the pledged property of all the above banks? A: It included all of them. It was the same.

Fengqi Company's cross-examination opinion on the record of the interrogation of Sun Jiaguo by the Economic Crime Investigation Detachment of the Changchun Public Security Bureau on September 18, 2014, was: Fengqi Company objected to the authenticity and legality of this record because it was not stamped by the public security organ. From the content, Sun Jiaguo did not have the qualifications to be a witness; Sun Jiaguo was an employee of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company and had an interest in this case, thus did not meet the requirements to be a witness. According to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Rules of Evidence, witnesses should appear in court to be questioned by the parties; otherwise, their testimony cannot be used as witness testimony.

Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's cross-examination opinion on the record of the interrogation of Sun Jiaguo of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company by the Economic Crime Investigation Detachment of the Changchun Public Security Bureau on September 18, 2014 (copied from the case file of the Supreme People's Court (2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 155), was: Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company had no objection to the authenticity and legality of the record of Sun Jiaguo. However, during the preparation of this record, the case-handling police officers used inducement against Sun Jiaguo (page 4, lines 5 and third from last). As a result, Sun Jiaguo did not have a firm belief about the fact that there was no grain, yet he made speculative conclusions. The conclusion on the second line of page 4 was also a speculation about what the leaders said, and a conclusion made by himself. It was not an objective conclusion. Sun Jiaguo could not objectively prove that the leaders and staff of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company knew from the beginning that there was no grain.

Dalian Port Company's cross-examination opinion on the record of the interrogation of Sun Jiaguo by the Economic Crime Investigation Detachment of the Changchun Public Security Bureau on September 18, 2014, was: This interrogation record further indicated that there was no grain involved in this case at all. Dalian Port Company was completely unaware and had no connection with this case.

The court of first instance held: In light of Fengqi Company's claims and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's defenses, the issues in dispute in this case were: First, whether Dalian Grain Company should repay Fengqi Company the outstanding debt of RMB 263,200,000 and overdue interest at a monthly rate of 2%; second, the validity of the "Maximum Amount Pledge Contract for Movable Property" and whether Fengqi Company had the right to be repaid in priority from the proceeds of disposing of the pledged property; third, the validity of the "Agreement on Pledge of Movable Property Supervision" and whether Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should bear joint and several compensatory liability for the debts owed by Dalian Grain Company up to RMB 300,000,000.

(1) Regarding whether Dalian Grain Company should repay Fengqi Company the outstanding debt of RMB 263,200,000 and overdue interest at a monthly rate of 2%.

The claim transferred to Fengqi Company in this case arose from the "Loan Agreement" and "Loan Contract" signed between non-party Li Qi, Yang Yi, Huang Jian, Cui Yang and Dalian Grain Company and Guangde Company, and the "Debt Confirmation and Assignment Agreement" and "Agreement" signed respectively between these four individuals and Guangde Company, Grain Company, and Fengqi Company. The above agreements and contracts were the true expressions of intent of the parties signing them, and their contents did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and were valid contracts. After the signing of the "Loan Agreement" and "Loan Contract," the lenders Li Qi, Yang Yi, Huang Jian, and Cui Yang performed their lending obligations as agreed. After the performance period of the contracts expired, Dalian Grain Company failed to perform its repayment obligations as agreed, constituting a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability for breach.

Regarding the principal amount to be repaid in this case, Fengqi Company claimed RMB 263,200,000, based on the amount of the claim transferred as confirmed in the "Debt Confirmation and Assignment Agreement" and "Agreement" signed between each creditor and debtor Guangde Company and Dalian Grain Company. This amount included the loan principal of RMB 208,000,000 and interest and fees up to May 31, 2014. The parties had no objection to this, so the court supported Fengqi Company's claim for the principal portion of RMB 208,000,000 out of the RMB 263,200,000.

Regarding interest on the principal of RMB 208,000,000. Since this case was accepted before September 1, 2015, the applicable law at that time was Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Opinions on the Trial of Lending Cases by People's Courts," which provided that the interest rate for private lending could be appropriately higher than the bank interest rate, with specific details to be determined by local people's courts based on local conditions, but the maximum shall not exceed four times the interest rate for similar loans of banks (including the principal rate). Interest exceeding this limit would not be protected.

The RMB 208,000,000 was composed of four loans: RMB 100,000,000, RMB 60,000,000, RMB 45,000,000, and RMB 3,000,000. In the loan contracts for these four loans, there was no agreement on interest during the loan term. Pursuant to Article 211 of the Contract Law of the PRC, if a contract for loan between natural persons does not stipulate the payment of interest or the stipulation is unclear, it shall be deemed that no interest is payable. The court did not support interest during the loan term for the four loans. Regarding overdue interest for the four loans, the contracts stipulated: 1. For the loan of RMB 100,000,000, the parties agreed on a loan term from May 18, 2013, to May 27, 2013, with overdue interest payable at a daily rate of 4‰ (equivalent to an annual rate of 144%). At the time of this loan, the short-term (less than six months) loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China in 2013 was 5.6% per annum (four times this rate was 22.4% per annum). Therefore, the agreed daily rate of 4‰ already exceeded four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China. Fengqi Company now claims overdue interest at a monthly rate of 2% (annual rate of 24%), which also exceeds the limit of four times the rate. Therefore, the overdue interest for this loan should be calculated from May 28, 2013, until the date of actual payment at four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. The excess portion is not supported. 2. For the loan of RMB 60,000,000, the parties agreed on a loan term from December 27, 2013, to December 30, 2013, with overdue interest payable at a daily rate of 5‰ (equivalent to an annual rate of 180%). At the time of this loan, the short-term (less than six months) loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China in 2013 was 5.6% per annum (four times this rate was 22.4% per annum). Therefore, the agreed daily rate of 5‰ already exceeded four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China. Fengqi Company now claims overdue interest at a monthly rate of 2% (annual rate of 24%), which also exceeds the limit of four times the rate. Therefore, the overdue interest for this loan should be calculated from December 31, 2013, until the date of actual payment at four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. The excess portion is not supported. 3. For the loan of RMB 45,000,000, the parties agreed on a loan term from September 27, 2013, to October 18, 2013, with overdue interest payable at a daily rate of 4‰ (equivalent to an annual rate of 144%). At the time of this loan, the short-term (less than six months) loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China in 2013 was 5.6% per annum (four times this rate was 22.4% per annum). Therefore, the agreed daily rate of 4‰ already exceeded four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China. Fengqi Company now claims overdue interest at a monthly rate of 2% (annual rate of 24%), which also exceeds the limit of four times the rate. Therefore, the overdue interest for this loan should be calculated from October 19, 2013, until the date of actual payment at four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. The excess portion is not supported. 4. For the loan of RMB 3,000,000, the parties agreed on a loan term from May 12, 2014, to May 31, 2014, with overdue interest payable at a daily rate of 0.6‰ (equivalent to an annual rate of 21.6%). At the time of this loan, the short-term (less than six months) loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China in 2014 was 5.6% per annum (four times this rate was 22.4% per annum). Therefore, the agreed daily rate of 0.6‰ did not exceed four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China, which complied with the law. Therefore, the overdue interest for this loan should be calculated from June 1, 2014, to June 4, 2014, at a daily rate of 0.6‰. After Fengqi Company assigned this claim, the overdue interest was agreed to be calculated at a monthly rate of 2% (equivalent to an annual rate of 24%). Because this agreement exceeded four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China, the overdue interest for this loan should be calculated from June 5, 2014, until the date of actual payment at four times the comparable loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. The excess portion is not supported by the court.

(2) Regarding the validity of the "Maximum Amount Pledge Contract for Movable Property" and whether Fengqi Company has the right to be repaid in priority from the proceeds of disposing of the pledged property.

The "Maximum Amount Pledge Contract for Movable Property" signed between Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company was the true expression of intent of both parties, did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and was legally valid. Both parties should perform their contractual obligations as agreed. Based on existing evidence, when the court commissioned the Changchun Intermediate Court to investigate, Liu Youwen already admitted that at the time of signing the "Maximum Amount Pledge Contract for Movable Property" with Fengqi Company and thereafter, he did not provide the pledged property of 145,400 tons of corn. Sun Jiaguo of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, who was responsible for supervision, also confirmed that the pledged property, including the 140,000 to 150,000 tons of corn for Fengqi Company, did not exist at all. Fengqi Company repeatedly requested to inspect the pledged property, but was always prevaricated by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company with evidence such as ledgers and cargo location maps. Although Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company claimed during the trial that the pledged corn existed at the bulk grain terminal of Dalian Port Company, after Dalian Port Company was added as a third party in this case, it confirmed that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company had never stored this batch of corn at the bulk grain terminal. During the original first instance, when the court attempted to seal and preserve the pledged property based on leads provided by Fengqi Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, it was unable to seal it. Accordingly, existing evidence cannot prove that Dalian Grain Company delivered the pledged property of 145,400 tons of corn. Pursuant to Article 212 of the Property Law of the PRC, a pledge is established when the pledgor delivers the pledged property. The pledge in question was not established according to law, and Fengqi Company cannot enjoy the right to be repaid in priority from the proceeds of disposing of the pledged property. Therefore, the court cannot support Fengqi Company's claim for the right to be repaid in priority from the proceeds of disposing of the pledged property.

Because Dalian Grain Company failed to provide the pledged property of 145,400 tons of corn as agreed in the "Maximum Amount Pledge Contract for Movable Property," it constituted a breach of contract. Pursuant to Article 107 of the Contract Law of the PRC, if a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner that does not conform to the agreement, it shall bear liability for breach by continuing performance, taking remedial measures, or compensating for losses. Dalian Grain Company should compensate Fengqi Company for its losses. Based on existing evidence, Fengqi Company's losses are the principal and corresponding interest on the loan. The liability for breach of contract that Dalian Grain Company should bear for violating its repayment obligations competes with this liability for compensation. Therefore, the court will not separately rule on Dalian Grain Company's liability for compensation.

(3) Regarding the validity of the "Agreement on Pledge of Movable Property Supervision" and whether Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should bear joint and several compensatory liability for the debts owed by Grain Company up to RMB 300,000,000.

The "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement" signed among Fengqi Company, Dalian Grain Company, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company reflects the true intentions of the three parties and does not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations; therefore, it shall be valid. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's defense that the agreement is invalid or not yet effective lacks legal basis and is not adopted by this court. According to the terms of the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement", Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company’s obligations include supervising the pledgor, monitoring the pledged property, and overseeing the pledgor’s processes such as warehousing and withdrawal of the pledged property. Once any act in violation of the agreement is discovered, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall promptly stop it and report to Fengqi Company. Monitoring the pledged property means inspecting and verifying the name, quantity, etc., of the pledged property and promptly reporting the status of the pledged property to Fengqi Company. If the goods delivered by Dalian Grain Company and the actual inventory are inconsistent with the "Letter of Substituted Pledge", Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall not accept the goods or issue a "Notice of Receipt of Goods" and shall immediately notify Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company in writing. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall station supervisors at the supervision site to inspect, verify, and count the pledged property, obtain and record data on the status of the pledged property, monitor the pledged property, and promptly report any shortages or other abnormal conditions to Fengqi Company and Grain Company, and take appropriate and reasonable measures to stop and rectify them. During the supervision period, if the pledged property is reduced, damaged, deteriorated, lost, or otherwise affected that may impact Fengqi Company’s rights for any reason, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall notify Fengqi Company within 24 hours and take appropriate emergency measures. During the supervision period, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall accept Fengqi Company’s inquiries regarding the pledged property and related documents, accept Fengqi Company’s inspections of the pledged property, and provide necessary assistance. It is evident that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, as the supervisor of the pledged property entrusted by Fengqi Company, should first verify and inspect the pledged property. However, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, knowing that Dalian Grain Company had fundamentally not provided the pledged property of 145,400 tons of corn and had not transferred possession of the pledged property, failed to promptly report or notify Fengqi Company of this situation. Instead, it issued a "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property" and, when Fengqi Company inspected the pledged property, provided Fengqi Company with so-called ledgers, storage location charts, and other documents to prove the existence of the pledged property. This clearly violated the obligations stipulated in the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement", and thus Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract.

In Article 12(1) of the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement", Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company promised that if it caused losses to Fengqi Company under the following circumstances, it would bear compensation liability for Fengqi Company’s actual losses, and Fengqi Company would have priority in claiming compensation for its actual losses, including: where Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company violates the provisions of Article 4(4) of this agreement (during the supervision period, if the pledged property is reduced, damaged, deteriorated, lost, or otherwise affected that may impact Party A’s rights for any reason, Party C shall notify Party A and Grain Company within 24 hours and take appropriate emergency measures), failing to timely notify Fengqi Company and Grain Company or failing to take appropriate emergency measures; and other circumstances where Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company violates this agreement and causes losses to Fengqi Company. Now, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, as the supervisor, knowing that the 145,400 tons of corn fundamentally did not exist, failed to timely notify Fengqi Company, and even issued relevant evidence of the existence of the pledged property to prevaricate during Fengqi Company’s inspection. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall therefore bear compensation liability for the losses caused to Fengqi Company. However, because Dalian Grain Company is the primary debtor and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company is the supervisor, based on the principle of fairness, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall bear compensation liability within the scope of Dalian Grain Company’s inability to repay Fengqi Company’s debt, i.e., it shall bear supplementary compensation liability. Furthermore, since the pledged property of 145,400 tons of corn supervised by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was valued at 300 million yuan as pledge collateral at the time, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall bear compensation liability for losses caused by Dalian Grain Company’s inability to repay Fengqi Company’s debt within the scope of 300 million yuan. As for Fengqi Company’s claim that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall bear joint and several compensation liability, because it lacks factual and legal basis, this court does not support Fengqi Company’s claim for joint and several compensation liability against Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company.

Regarding Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company’s defense that the pledge contract between Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company in this case constitutes a pledge of rights, i.e., a warehouse receipt pledge rather than a pledge of movable property, and that it has fulfilled its responsibilities for the storage and safekeeping of documents without any breach of contract. According to the "Maximum Amount Movable Property Pledge Contract" signed between Fengqi Company and Grain Company, Dalian Grain Company provided the principal and interest of the loan as pledge collateral with its own corn. The pledged property involved in this case is the 145,400 tons of corn itself, not a pledge of corn warehouse receipts. Therefore, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company’s defense that it has fulfilled its responsibilities for document safekeeping without any breach of contract lacks factual and legal basis and is not adopted by this court.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 8, 52, 60(1), 79, 80, 81, 107, 196, 205, 206, 207, and 211 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 212 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 63 and 67 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on Issues Concerning the Trial of Lending Cases by People's Courts, and Articles 142 and 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: (1) Dalian Grain Company shall repay Fengqi Company the loan principal of 208 million yuan and overdue interest (calculation of overdue interest: for the first tranche of 100 million yuan, from May 28, 2013; for the second tranche of 60 million yuan, from December 31, 2013; for the third tranche of 45 million yuan, from October 19, 2013, until the actual date of full payment, all calculated at four times the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period and type; for the fourth tranche of 3 million yuan, from June 1 to June 4, 2014, calculated at a daily interest rate of 0.6‰, and from June 5, 2014, until the actual date of full payment, calculated at four times the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period and type); if the above obligor fails to perform the monetary payment obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall double the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. (2) Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of 300 million yuan for Dalian Grain Company’s repayment obligation under Item (1) of this judgment; (3) Fengqi Company’s other claims are dismissed. The court costs for the first instance are 1,397,280 yuan, and the property preservation fee is 5,000 yuan, totaling 1,402,280 yuan, to be jointly borne by Dalian Grain Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company.

Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed to this court, arguing: (1) The original judgment erred in finding the facts. First, the determination of the debt involved was erroneous. The transfer of the 3 million yuan debt from Cui Yang and the 60 million yuan debt from Huang Jian to Fengqi Company was supported only by payment vouchers provided by Fengqi Company, i.e., business vouchers/receipts from Shanghai Pudong Development Bank. However, these receipts are insufficient to prove that Dalian Grain Company received these two loans, and Fengqi Company’s 63 million yuan claim against Dalian Grain Company cannot be established. Second, Fengqi Company knew that the pledged property did not exist from the beginning. The interrogation record of Liu Youwen can affect the characterization of the case and the allocation of responsibilities among the parties. This interrogation record confirms that Fengqi Company knew from the start that the pledged property did not exist and should bear its own responsibility. Evidence such as the waybills, measurement sheets, quality inspection reports, warehouse entry receipts, and storage location charts proves that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company has fulfilled its obligation to review documents as stipulated in the contract. The original judgment’s failure to admit this evidence and its conclusion that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company knew from the beginning that there was no pledged property were erroneous.

(2) The original judgment erred in ordering Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company to bear compensation liability. The pledge right is established upon the delivery of the pledged property by the pledgor. Dalian Grain Company made a false pledge, and the pledge right involved was not established. In the absence of the pledged property, the supervision agreement with that property as the subject of supervision cannot be performed from the outset due to the failure to achieve the contract’s purpose. During supervision, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company fulfilled its obligations of surface review, visual inspection, and document verification. At the same time, according to Articles 2.2 and 2.3 of the supervision agreement, Fengqi Company knew that the authenticity of the goods and documents was the responsibility of Dalian Grain Company and knew that the contract terms explicitly provided that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company did not guarantee or assume liability for the authenticity of the pledged property’s quality, ownership, or value. Therefore, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should not bear compensation liability, and the original judgment applied the law incorrectly.

(3) The original judgment erred in handling this case as a civil case; it should have been transferred to the public security authorities. The facts of Dalian Grain Company’s false pledge are clear and constitute a crime. Regardless of whether Fengqi Company knew that the pledged property did not exist from the beginning, this case should be transferred to the public security authorities for handling in accordance with the law.

The appellee, Fengqi Company, argued in defense: (1) The original judgment correctly found the facts. First, the determination of the 208 million yuan debt involved was clear and supported by sufficient evidence. The "Debt Confirmation and Assignment Agreement" and the "Agreement" were examined during the first-instance trial and were admitted by all parties. The first-instance court’s confirmation that Fengqi Company had a claim of 208 million yuan in principal and interest against Grain Company was based on facts and law. Second, Fengqi Company did not know that the pledged property did not exist from the beginning. On the day the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement" was signed, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company refused Fengqi Company’s request for inspection. During the supervision period, Fengqi Company went to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company four times to inquire about the status of the pledged property. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company showed Fengqi Company ledgers, storage location charts, general ledgers, subsidiary ledgers, and other materials to prove that the pledged property was intact. Based on the evidence provided by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, Fengqi Company believed that the pledged property existed.

(2) The original judgment’s order that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company bear compensation liability was not improper. Articles 2, 3, 4, and 5 of the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement" stipulated Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company’s obligations to verify and monitor the pledged property, as well as its notification obligations. As the supervisor, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company had the duty to inspect the pledged property. Knowing that Dalian Grain Company had not provided the pledged property and had not transferred possession of it, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company failed to promptly report or notify Fengqi Company of this situation. Instead, it still issued a "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property" and, when Fengqi Company requested an inspection, provided ledgers, storage location charts, and other materials to prove the existence of the pledged property, violating the obligations stipulated in the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement". The original judgment’s order that it bear compensation liability was correct.

(3) This case should continue to be heard as a civil case. According to Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Certain Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Crime Suspicions in Economic Dispute Cases, this case should continue to be heard. Whether the employees of Dalian Grain Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company committed a crime does not affect the civil liability of Dalian Grain Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company as civil entities.

The third party in the original trial, Dalian Port Company, argued: Dalian Port Company has no connection to this case.

The facts as found by this court upon trial are consistent with those found by the original trial court.

This court holds that, based on the appeal and defense opinions of the parties and the facts found, the disputed issues in this case are: First, the amount of Fengqi Company’s debt involved; Second, whether Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should bear compensation liability for the losses caused by the failure to establish the pledge right involved in Fengqi Company’s case, the nature of that liability, and how it should be borne; Third, whether this case should be transferred to the public security authorities.

(I) The principal amount of Fengqi Company’s debt involved should be determined as 208 million yuan.

Regarding the issue of the 3 million yuan debt from Cui Yang and the 60 million yuan debt from Huang Jian that were assigned to Fengqi Company: First, the "Loan Contracts" between Cui Yang, Huang Jian, and Dalian Grain Company were actually performed. On December 26, 2013, Huang Jian and Dalian Grain Company signed a "Loan Contract" stipulating a loan amount of 60 million yuan, and on December 27, 2013, the funds were remitted through Shanghai Pudong Development Bank to the account designated by Dalian Grain Company. On May 12, 2014, Cui Yang and Dalian Grain Company signed a "Loan Contract" stipulating a loan amount of 3 million yuan. On the day the contract was signed, Cui Yang remitted the funds through Shanghai Pudong Development Bank to the account designated by Dalian Grain Company. The dates, remitters, payees, and remittance amounts indicated on the banking business vouchers/receipts for the above two loans are consistent with the corresponding "Loan Contracts", and all bear the bank’s business accounting seal, sufficiently proving that Huang Jian and Cui Yang fulfilled their lending obligations after the contracts were signed.

Second, the claims of Cui Yang and Huang Jian against Dalian Grain Company were confirmed and then assigned to Fengqi Company. On May 31, 2014, Yang Yi and Huang Jian as Party A, Guangde Company and Dalian Grain Company as Party B, and Fengqi Company as Party C jointly signed the "Debt Confirmation and Assignment Agreement", which confirmed that Huang Jian had lent 60 million yuan to Dalian Grain Company on December 27, 2013, and agreed to assign this claim to Fengqi Company. On June 1, 2014, Cui Yang as Party A, Dalian Grain Company as Party B, and Fengqi Company as Party C signed an "Agreement", confirming that Dalian Grain Company had borrowed 3 million yuan from Cui Yang on May 12, 2014, and Cui Yang agreed to assign this claim to Fengqi Company. The "Debt Confirmation and Assignment Agreement" and the "Agreement" reflect the true intentions of the parties, and their contents do not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations; they are valid contracts. In these agreements, creditors Huang Jian and Cui Yang and debtor Dalian Grain Company confirmed the loan amounts and agreed to assign the claims to Fengqi Company. Therefore, Fengqi Company lawfully holds a claim of 63 million yuan against Dalian Grain Company. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company’s appeal request that these two claims are not established lacks factual and legal basis. The original judgment’s determination of the principal debt involved as 208 million yuan is supported by evidence.

(II) Dalian Grain Company, Fengqi Company, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company all bear fault for the losses caused by the failure to establish the pledge right involved, and all should bear responsibility.

According to Article 212 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, the pledge right is established upon the delivery of the pledged property by the pledgor. In this case, Dalian Grain Company and Fengqi Company signed the "Maximum Amount Movable Property Pledge Contract", which was formed and became effective. However, Dalian Grain Company never delivered the pledged property of 145,400 tons of corn, and the pledge right was not established. For the losses caused to Fengqi Company due to the failure to establish the pledge right, the responsible parties shall bear corresponding liability based on the degree of fault of Dalian Grain Company, Fengqi Company, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company.

First, as for Dalian Grain Company: According to Article 63 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, Dalian Grain Company should have delivered the pledged corn to Fengqi Company in accordance with the law. The "Maximum Amount Movable Property Pledge Contract" signed between Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company stipulated that Dalian Grain Company voluntarily used its own 145,400 tons of corn as pledge collateral for the debt involved, and Dalian Grain Company should have delivered the pledged property (including accessories), relevant title documents, and materials required for safekeeping to Fengqi Company on the date the contract was signed. Article 2.1 of the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement" signed by Fengqi Company, Dalian Grain Company, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company stipulated that the pledged property is the subject of the pledge, i.e., the goods agreed upon in the pledge contract signed between Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company, which are to be provided by Dalian Grain Company as pledge collateral to Fengqi Company and placed under the supervision of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. Article 2.2 stipulated that Dalian Grain Company guarantees that the name, specifications, model, manufacturer (place of origin), quantity, quality, packaging, number of pieces, and marks of the pledged property are consistent with those agreed with Fengqi Company and those declared and delivered to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, and that Dalian Grain Company bears legal liability for the truthfulness of all the above facts. According to the above stipulations, Dalian Grain Company should have delivered 145,400 tons of pledged corn to Fengqi Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. The legal representative of Dalian Grain Company, Liu Youwen, was detained on suspicion of contract fraud. Since his criminal case was being heard by the Changchun Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Changchun Intermediate Court) during the first instance, the first-instance court commissioned the Changchun Intermediate Court to interrogate Liu Youwen. During the interrogation, he admitted that Dalian Grain Company had not provided the pledged corn as agreed after signing the contract with Fengqi Company, and that the pledged property involved did not exist from the beginning. Thus, the pledged property involved was not actually delivered. The party obligated to deliver the pledged property, Dalian Grain Company, must have been aware of the fact that the pledged property did not exist from the beginning. According to Article 86 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, if the debtor or a third party fails to deliver the pledged property within the time limit agreed in the pledge contract, thereby causing losses to the pledgee, the pledgor shall bear compensation liability based on its fault. In this case, Dalian Grain Company, knowing that the pledged corn had not been delivered, still issued the "Letter of Substituted Pledge" together with Fengqi Company to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, confirming the weight, inventory, and other information of the pledged corn, demonstrating clear subjective fault. Since the delivery of the pledged property directly determines the establishment of the pledge right, without the pledged property, the pledge right cannot be established. Since Dalian Grain Company did not actually deliver the pledged property, it should bear primary responsibility for the losses caused to Fengqi Company due to the non-existence of the pledged property from the beginning and the consequent failure to establish the pledge right. Although Dalian Grain Company is the pledgor of the pledged corn involved, it is also the debtor, and in principle, it should bear repayment responsibility for the entire debt involved. Its liability for breach of contract as a party to the "Maximum Amount Movable Property Pledge Contract" and as a related party to the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Contract" merges with its liability as a debtor, which will not be further elaborated here.

Second, as for Fengqi Company: First, Article 6.1 of the "Maximum Amount Movable Property Pledge Contract" stipulates that the pledged property under the contract shall be possessed and managed by Dalian Grain Company, and Dalian Grain Company shall deliver the pledged property, relevant title documents, and materials required for safekeeping to the pledgee, Fengqi Company, on the date the contract is signed. The preamble of the "Dynamic Pledge Supervision Agreement" stipulates that both Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company agree to place the pledged property under the supervision of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company agrees to accept Fengqi Company’s entrustment and supervise the pledged property in accordance with Fengqi Company’s instructions. According to the above contractual stipulations, the pledged property involved should first be delivered by Dalian Grain Company to Fengqi Company, and then Fengqi Company should deliver it to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company for supervision. Before delivery to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, Dalian Grain Company should have delivered the pledged supervised property to Fengqi Company in accordance with the pledge contract, and Fengqi Company should have possessed it. Therefore, Fengqi Company knew or should have known whether the pledged property existed before delivering it to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company for supervision.

Second, Article 215 of the Property Law of the PRC provides that the pledgee has the obligation to properly keep the pledged property. In this case, Fengqi Company, as the pledgee, had the obligation to inspect and keep the pledged property, and should have strictly examined the pledged property delivered by the debtor Dalian Grain Company. However, Fengqi Company failed to perform the corresponding obligation, but instead delegated this obligation entirely to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company through the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Contract." Fengqi Company neither inspected the actual inventory of the pledged property nor urged Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company to conduct inspection in accordance with the supervision contract. On the same day as signing the "Maximum Amount Choses in Possession Pledge Contract," it issued to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company the "Notice of Substituted Pledge," which bore its company seal and the seal of its legal representative. This notice not only recorded the name, place of origin, and weight of the pledged property, but also recorded the inventory status of the goods. On the one hand, this act showed that Fengqi Company knew or should have known whether the pledged property was in the warehouse; on the other hand, it also indicated that not only did it neglect its statutory obligation to inspect the pledged property, but it also poorly managed the realization of its claims and allowed the risk of non-recovery to expand. Fengqi Company itself was clearly at fault for the loss caused by the fact that the pledged property never existed, resulting in the pledge right not being established, and should also bear corresponding liability.

Third, with regard to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. First, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was at fault for the loss caused to Fengqi Company due to the non-establishment of the pledge right. On the one hand, the "Maximum Amount Choses in Possession Pledge Contract" between Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company was signed on June 4, 2014. On the same day, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, Fengqi Company, and Dalian Grain Company signed the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement." Also on the same day, Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company issued the "Notice of Substituted Pledge" to Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company issued the "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property" on June 4, 2014. The pledged property in question was 145,400 metric tons of corn, a huge quantity that would require substantial manpower, materials, and time to actually inspect, verify, and count. However, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company issued the "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property" on the same day as signing the supervision agreement, confirming that the pledged property was under its possession and supervision. Such a short time period clearly indicated that no counting or verification of the pledged property had been conducted. On the other hand, Sun Jiaguo, a supervisor of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, admitted in his interrogation that he had handled the supervision of 140,000 to 150,000 metric tons of corn pledged by Fengqi Company. During the supervision period, acting on instructions from his superiors, he fabricated the supervision log and detailed ledger accounts, knowing that there was no grain in the warehouse and not knowing the specific location of the grain storage positions, to prove that the grain existed and was under supervision. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company acknowledged this testimony. Liu Youwen, the legal representative of Dalian Grain Company, also stated in his interrogation that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company knew that the pledged property of 145,400 metric tons of corn had never existed from the beginning. Sun Jiaguo and Liu Youwen belong to different entities, and Sun Jiaguo is an employee of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. Their testimonies both proved that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company knew the fact that the pledged property at issue never existed. In conclusion, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company knew or should have known that the pledged property of 145,400 metric tons of corn did not exist. Under such circumstances, it still provided so-called supervision, and was clearly at fault for the loss caused to Fengqi Company by the non-establishment of the pledge right.

Second, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company breached its contractual obligations under the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement." Article 369 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides that the bailee shall properly keep the bailed property. Article 399 provides that the agent shall handle the entrusted affairs in accordance with the instructions of the principal. Article 401 provides that the agent shall report on the handling of the entrusted affairs as required by the principal. Article 1 of the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement" in this case stipulates that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall supervise the pledgor, monitor the pledged property, and supervise the pledgor's processes such as warehousing and withdrawal of the pledged property. Once any act violating the agreement is discovered, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall promptly stop it and report to Fengqi Company. Monitoring of the pledged property means verifying and checking the name, quantity, etc. of the pledged property, and promptly reporting the status of the pledged property to Fengqi Company. Article 2.8 stipulates that if the goods delivered by Dalian Grain Company and the actual inventory are inconsistent with what is recorded in the "Notice of Substituted Pledge," Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall not accept the goods or issue a "Notice of Receipt of Goods," and shall immediately notify Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company in writing. Article 4.1 stipulates that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall station supervisors at the supervision site to inspect, verify, and count the pledged property, obtain and record data on the status of the pledged property; monitor the pledged property, and promptly report to Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company upon discovering any shortage or other abnormal conditions, and require Dalian Grain Company to take measures to stop or correct them. Article 4.4 stipulates that during the supervision period, if for any reason the pledged property becomes short, damaged, deteriorated, lost, or other circumstances that may affect Fengqi Company's rights and interests, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall notify Fengqi Company within 24 hours and take appropriate emergency measures. Article 4.6 stipulates that during the supervision period, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall accept Fengqi Company's inquiries concerning the pledged property and related documents, accept Fengqi Company's inspection of the pledged property, and provide necessary assistance. In this case, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, as a professional supervisor, should first have verified and inspected the pledged property at issue. However, it disregarded the provisions of the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement." Without actually inspecting the delivery status and actual inventory of the pledged property, it casually issued the "Notice of Receipt of Pledged Property" on the same day as signing the supervision agreement, and failed to promptly report or notify Fengqi Company of this situation. When Fengqi Company inspected the pledged property, it provided Fengqi Company with so-called ledgers, warehouse location charts, etc. to prove the existence of the pledged property. These acts of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company clearly violated the obligations stipulated in the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement." Since Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company was at fault for the loss caused to Fengqi Company by the non-establishment of the pledge right, and this fault act violated the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement," it should also bear corresponding liability for this loss.

In summary, because the pledgor Dalian Grain Company, the pledgee Fengqi Company, and the supervisor Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company were all at fault for the non-establishment of the pledge right at issue, all three parties should bear corresponding liability. Furthermore, as the entity that delivered the pledged property, Dalian Grain Company bears primary liability. This Court holds that the responsibility share of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company, as the supervisor of the pledged property, for the loss caused to Fengqi Company by the non-establishment of the pledge right at issue, should not exceed 30%.

(III) The nature and manner of liability undertaken by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company in this case.

First, the nature of the liability undertaken by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should be liability for breach of contract. Liability for breach of contract refers to the civil liability a party to a contract bears for failing to perform its contractual obligations or for performing them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement. Article 107 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides that if a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, it shall bear liability for breach of contract, such as continuing performance, taking remedial measures, or compensating for losses. In this case, the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement" stipulates that Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall, as required by Fengqi Company, verify the title and quality certification documents of the pledged property; verify the goods delivered by Dalian Grain Company and the existing inventory in accordance with the contents listed in the "Notice of Substituted Pledge"; and during the supervision period, if for any reason the pledged property becomes short, damaged, deteriorated, lost, or other circumstances that may affect Fengqi Company's rights and interests, it shall notify Fengqi Company within 24 hours and take appropriate emergency measures. However, Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company failed to perform its obligations to inspect, verify, and count the pledged property and its obligation to report as stipulated in the contract, resulting in the failure to establish Fengqi Company's pledge right because the pledged property never existed. It should bear corresponding liability for the loss of Fengqi Company's claims caused by the non-establishment of the pledge right. This liability arises from the breach of contractual obligations and is in nature liability for breach of contract.

Second, the manner in which Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company undertakes liability should be supplementary compensation liability. In the legal relationship of claims, debts, and security, the debtor is the ultimate obligor. The guarantor, after substituting the debtor in satisfying the claim, may seek recourse against the debtor. The guarantor is a secondary obligor, arising by law or agreement, and is a direct obligor to the creditor. Compared to the debtor and the guarantor, the supervisor of the collateral is merely an assistant helping the creditor realize the claim, not a direct obligor for the realization of the claim. Although its liability has a certain independence, except for the loss of the supervised collateral caused by its own actions, its liability must be attached to the direct liability of the debtor and the guarantor. If the direct liability is extinguished by performance, the creditor suffers no loss due to satisfaction, and thus the supervisor's liability is correspondingly extinguished. Therefore, it can only be an auxiliary, supplementary obligor after the aforementioned direct obligors. In practice, this is even more appropriate in the following two situations. First, the claim arises earlier and has already fallen into the risk of non-recovery. In such a situation, the risk of non-recovery of the claim arises earlier, while the supervision of the collateral appears later. The claim is not generated because of trust in the guarantee of the pledge right or the supervision of the collateral by the supervisor. The primary reason for the failure to realize the claim is the debtor's inability to satisfy the claim, which does not have a direct causal relationship with the subsequent entry of the collateral supervisor. Second, the creditor and the guarantor are at fault for the non-establishment of the pledge right, and their fault occurred first. In such a situation, besides the debtor's inability to satisfy the claim, the primary reason for the failure to realize the claim is the prior fault of the creditor and the guarantor leading to the non-establishment of the pledge right. Therefore, the subsequent entry of the collateral supervisor cannot fundamentally affect the fact that the pledge right could not be established. In the above two situations, the liability of the collateral supervisor should only be auxiliary and supplementary.

In this case, on the one hand, the original claims in this case had already been formed in May, September, and December 2013, and May 2014, and had all exceeded the agreed repayment period without being satisfied. Even for Fengqi Company, which acquired these original claims, a considerable part of its claims were acquired before June 4, 2014, when the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement" at issue was signed. The risk of non-recovery of the claims at issue arose before the signing of the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement," and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company's supervision of the pledged property at issue occurred later. The claims at issue were not generated because of trust in the pledge guarantee provided by Dalian Grain Company or the supervision of the pledged property by Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company. The primary reason for their non-recovery was the inability of the debtor Dalian Grain Company to satisfy the claims, which does not have a direct causal relationship with the subsequent entry of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company as the collateral supervisor. On the other hand, the pledge right of Fengqi Company in this case could not be established because the pledged property never existed from the beginning. The primary reason was the prior false pledge by the debtor Dalian Grain Company and the creditor Fengqi Company's fault in examining the debtor's false pledge. The subsequent entry of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company as the collateral supervisor merely continued this state of false pledge; it was not the supervisory act of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company that directly caused the false pledge. Therefore, the liability of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company should be ranked after the direct liability of the debtor Dalian Grain Company and related guarantors, and the manner of liability should be determined as supplementary compensation liability. The specific amount of loss of Fengqi Company's claims can only be determined after the People's Court enforces against the debtor Dalian Grain Company and other guarantors. Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion that remains unsatisfied after the People's Court enforces against Dalian Grain Company and other guarantors and exhausts all enforcement measures.

(IV) This case should not be transferred to the public security authority for handling.

Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Suspected Economic Crimes stipulates that if the same citizen, legal person, or other economic organization is involved in both economic disputes and suspected economic crimes due to different legal facts, the economic dispute case and the suspected economic crime case shall be tried separately. In this case, there are two legal relationships: one is the legal relationship of claims, debts, and security. The legal relationship of claims and debts was formed through the transfer of claims based on the "Loan Agreements" and "Loan Contracts" signed by third parties Li Qi, Yang Yi, Huang Jian, and Cui Yang with Dalian Grain Company and Guangde Company, and the "Debt Confirmation and Claims Transfer Agreements" and "Agreements" signed by these four persons respectively with Guangde Company, Dalian Grain Company, and Fengqi Company. The security legal relationship was formed by signing the "Maximum Amount Choses in Possession Pledge Contract." The subjects of the claims, debts, and security legal relationship are the creditor and pledgee Fengqi Company and the debtor and pledgor Dalian Grain Company. The other legal relationship is the choses in possession pledge supervision legal relationship, based on the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement," with the principal Fengqi Company and the agent Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company as the contractual subjects. The primary legal relationship tried in this case is the contractual relationship formed between Fengqi Company and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company based on the "Choses in Possession Pledge Supervision Agreement." The choses in possession supervision legal relationship between Fengqi Company as the principal and Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company as the agent, and the claims, debts, and security legal relationship between Fengqi Company and Dalian Grain Company, not only have different subjects and different rights and obligations, but also are not based on the same legal facts. Therefore, whether Dalian Grain Company and its legal representative are suspected of economic crimes based on the loan and guarantee facts does not share the same identity with the choses in possession pledge supervision contractual relationship tried in this case. This case, as a civil case, shall continue to be tried. The appeal request of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company that this case should be transferred to the public security authority for handling because Dalian Grain Company and its legal representative are suspected of economic crimes lacks factual and legal basis and should not be supported.

In conclusion, the appeal grounds of Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company in this case, that it has performed its contractual obligations in accordance with the contract and should not bear compensation liability and that this case should not be handled as a civil case, lack factual and legal basis and are not supported by this Court. The original judgment ordering Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company to bear supplementary compensation liability for the compensation liability that Dalian Grain Company should bear within the scope of RMB 300 million was improper and is hereby corrected by this Court in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, items (1) and (2), and Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm items 1 and 3 of the Civil Judgment of Liaoning High People's Court (2016) Liao Min Chu Zi No. 1;

2. Amend item 2 of the Civil Judgment of Liaoning High People's Court (2016) Liao Min Chu Zi No. 1 to: Sinotrans Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability not exceeding 30% for the portion of Fengqi Company's claims that remains unsatisfied after the People's Court enforces against the debtor Dalian Harbor Grain Co., Ltd. and other guarantors.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,397,280 and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Dalian Harbor Grain Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 981,596 and by Sinotrans Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company in the amount of RMB 420,684; the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,397,280 shall be borne by Dalian Harbor Grain Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 978,096 and by Sinotrans Liaoning Storage and Transportation Company in the amount of RMB 419,184.
